correctness.rationale: The claim is proved by two exact finite certificates. The 21-word construction covers all 81 length-four ternary targets. Independently, a nonnegative dual weight on those 81 targets has total \(468/23\), and exact enumeration of all 243 length-five centers verifies deletion-ball weight at most one. The covering inequality then forces every code to have at least \(\lceil468/23\rceil=21\) words. Definitions use distinct deletion descendants, all quantifiers are finite and exhausted, and no floating-point result is used in the proof.

value.rationale: \(\mathsf K_{\mathsf D}^{q}(n,R)\) is the minimum-cardinality invariant introduced in the primary deletion-covering literature. The ternary length-five radius-one case is a natural small nonbinary benchmark where published general bounds are nonexact. The certificate is structurally informative rather than a table recomputation: nonuniform orbit weights capture the irregular deletion-ball sizes highlighted by the foundational method, while the matching 21-word construction closes the finite gap exactly.
